title: A Parallel Hybrid CNN–Transformer Model for Brain Tumor Classification in MRI Images
content: Brain tumors are among the most life-threatening neurological disorders, and early, accurate diagnosis using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for effective treatment planning. This study proposes a parallel hybrid CNN Transformer architecture that integrates a ResNet50 backbone enhanced with a Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) for local feature refinement, alongside a Swin-Tiny Transformer for capturing global contextual dependencies. The two branches are fused through feature concatenation, followed by Layer Normalization and a fully connected classification head. The proposed model was evaluated on a publicly available, four-class brain tumor MRI data set comprising glioma, meningioma, pituitary, and No Tumor classes. The data set was divided into training, validation, and testing sets using a 70%, 15%, and 15% split, respectively, ensuring robust model training and unbiased performance evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate high performance, achieving 98.26% accuracy in multi class classification and 99.42% accuracy in binary tumor detection, with a specificity of 99.79%. Furthermore, Grad-CAM-based visualizations confirm that the model focuses on clinically relevant tumor regions, enhancing interpretability and clinical trust. These results indicate that the proposed approach is a reliable and effective solution for computer-aided brain tumor diagnosis, particularly in resource-constrained healthcare environments.
